gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-merriweather-san: Merriweather Sans stands tall and sturdy, its lowercase big and its e opening clearly to the right, so every word looks sized up. Against Bushcraft's wide-spaced, curve-flat letters, that openness is the pair's whole appeal.
gen-gf-revalia-archivo: Archivo brings curves that open outward and an x-height with real authority, giving Revalia's bold, widely spaced display letters something sturdy to stand on. And a modest bump in the body size would let that tall lowercase hold its own.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-epilogue: Epilogue is curvy and loose, with a tall lowercase, stubby ascender tips and a wire-thin monoline skeleton that feels contemporary. But Early GameBoy tapers slightly where its strokes turn, so the heading looks playful and punchy over that thin, even line.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-archivo: Stencil swagger, front and center. Snowburst One cuts wide bridges through tall letters, and Archivo follows with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height that keep the sans-serif text easy to settle into.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-fs-asap: Stencil bridges and tall lowercase make Snowburst One loud on sight, while Asap's open-arc c forms keep the sans-serif text readable. Its lowercase nearly matches the capitals in height, and that is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-nordic-switzer: Ancient and powerful, Nordic sets tight, folded openings in a stroke that never changes width. Switzer then works against it, with wire-like letters, a tall waist line and c tips that stay well apart, so the page gets both weight and air.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-public-sans: Origami looks like a sign-painter's single brush stroke, its lowercase dense as poured lead type, while Public Sans sits below with a hefty body and broad open counters. Long text would feel sturdy and easy to follow.
gen-dafont-nasalization-fs-merriweather-: Friendly and spaced-out, with short ascenders and a big lowercase. Nasalization floats its letters apart, but Merriweather Sans packs sturdy, tall sans-serif words beneath it, and its e opens clearly to the right.
gen-dafont-stentiga-satoshi: Satoshi lifts its lowercase high and leaves the e wide open, every stroke cut to a single width. Stentiga's luxurious, spread-out letters sit above it, and the two share an unhurried, spacious feel.
gen-dafont-college-manrope: Authority with a bounce: College draws every curve as thick as a straight stem, and its big counters sit in a tall lowercase. And Manrope's bright, open curves and minimal cap-to-lowercase step make the sans-serif text glide along.
